# Step 2.148: the takeover question, and "Send these plays" (handover)

## Builder 1 (server and the controller's logic), 2026-11-24

- **The rule** (`packages/core/src/modules/games/scoring-session.ts`): `openFor` takes a `ScorableGame` (`{ id, underWay }`, under way = live on the server, a reopened game too). A lapsed holder of a game under way is answered `held-by-other`, never displaced; same device and account carries on; a game not live still opens once the holder lapsed. `take-over-scoring.ts` takes a lapsed holder of a game under way only with the matching `expectedHolderSince`, and logs it. Mark not started (2.121) untouched.
- **The question's facts**: `ScoringHolder.lastHeardAt` (lease's last writing, up to ~30 s early) and `sameAccount` (server's mark); the reply's `Holder` (`packages/contracts/src/tracker-protocol.ts`) carries `lastHeardAt?` and `sameAccount?: true`; `apps/web/src/server/scoring-session-endpoint.ts` passes them on.
- **"Send these plays"**: `CommandBatch.notSavedSince` (version 2 only) through the same commands door; `packages/core/src/modules/games/game-moved-since.ts` decides; new refusal code `game-moved`. New query `packages/database/src/queries/list-game-events-after.ts` (port `LiveGamesStore.eventsAfter`, league-fenced). No migration.
- **The controller** (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/tracker-controller.ts`): the "asked" state is the existing `mode.kind === 'held-by-other'` (action `takeOver()`), its `holder` now with `lastHeardAt?`/`sameAccount?`. New `status().sendNotSaved`: `'none' | 'offered' | 'sending' | 'game-moved'`, and `controller.sendNotSaved()` → `{ ok: true, saved }` or `not-offered | game-moved | unanswered | refused`. "Enter again" is the existing `enterAgain(id)` (S-77, only while holding).
- **Decisions**: `docs/specs/v1/decisions-pending/T-335.md` (how the server knows the game has not moved), `T-336.md` (under way, the facts). T6 §5 corrected; P7 §5.2 already said it.
- **Tests**: `open-scoring-session.test.ts` and `take-over-scoring.test.ts` (new describes: ten minutes silent, same account marked, same device carries on, not started opens, no permission, quiet holder taken only on yes), `game-moved-since.test.ts` (twenty plays once and in order, second send none, one play in between refuses all, lost answer counted once, End and reopen by the same scorekeeper, another's End counts, unknown sequence, other maker, no permission, version 1), `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts` (over the endpoints).
- **Expectations changed** (shape only, no weakening): four `held-by-other` replies compared whole now include `lastHeardAt` and `sameAccount: false` (open ×3, take-over ×1, `packages/database/src/stores/scoring-sessions-commands.test.ts` ×1); "same account on another device" now also expects `sameAccount: true`; two test names now say "not yet started" for the lapsed give-away, which still holds for such a game.
- **Run and passed**: `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, vitest of `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/contracts/src`, `apps/web/src/features/tracker` (723 + 4), `packages/database/src/isolation` with the scoring-sessions, tracker-commands, mark-not-started and role-matrix store tests (632), `node scripts/fence-filter-check.mjs list-game-events-after` (caught), the pending-decisions test. New isolation case for `listGameEventsAfter`. Not run by me: `apps/web/src/server` as a folder (result in the report), the whole unit run.

## For builder 2

- Words and buttons: the question ("{name} was scoring, last heard from {n} minutes ago"; "you, on another device" when `holder.sameAccount`), "Yes, take over"; on the read-only device "Send these plays" while `sendNotSaved === 'offered'`, "Sending…", and after `game-moved` a plain line that each play is entered again by whoever holds the game. Messages in `packages/site/src/messages/en/` files (rule 16).
- Pictures, the browser test with two devices and a controlled clock (the plan's done test: ten minutes silent, "last heard from 10 minutes ago", Yes, twenty sent once, one in between refuses), page-step checks, the whole chain.

## What I distrust

- A tracker opened before this release fails to read a `held-by-other` reply with the new fields (strict schema): a release should not land during a takeover.
- The device knows `notSavedSince` only for a loss on that page; after a reload only "Enter again". A second loss keeps the first sequence (refuses more, never counts twice).
- After a send is taken while another device holds the game, that device's screen does not reload by itself until its next refusal or load: its score may lag. Worth a look in the browser test.
- A game not live (line-ups only) whose holder went quiet is still given away; plays it made offline then list as not saved, and "Send these plays" works if nothing was recorded since.

## Builder 2 (the screen, the lead's two decisions, the browser test), 2026-11-24

- **The screen** (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/take-over-parts.tsx`, wired in `tracker-opening.tsx`): on opening a held game the notice names the holder, or says "You are scoring this game on another device." by the server's `sameAccount` mark; under it "That device was last heard from {n} minutes ago" (server clock via `status().now()`, re-read every 15 s). The question says "from you, on another device" by the mark, and its text now says unsent plays can be sent until something is recorded. The not-saved list shows "Send these plays" while `offered`, "Sending…" (disabled), and after `game-moved` a plain line, no button. Words in `packages/site/src/messages/en/tracker.ts`. Tests: `take-over-parts.test.ts`. No pictures: the lane's other screens have none.
- **T-337** (decided by the lead): the sequence is kept with each not-saved tap (`notSavedSince` on the stored entry, through `QueueSettlement` and `queue.setAside(ids, since)`), under the same person-bound keeping; after a reload the offer stands on the earliest sequence named, and the batch names the plays' own session. T-335 and T6 §5 corrected.
- **T-338** (decided by the lead): found by test that the holding device showed a stale game after another's plays were sent (laptop 0:2 while the server had 6:2). Now a batch answered with a sequence beyond base plus its own taps loads the state again (`loadAgain`, shared with the refusal path).
- **Unit tests**: `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts` now starts the clock (a game under way), keeps storage person-bound (`inLeague`, as the page does), and has the reload case (another account on the device sees none, the same one sends three once) and the holder case; both failed before their fixes. Storage contract: the sequence kept per tap. The old "not offered after a reload" test was replaced by the lead's decision, not weakened.
- **Browser test** `tests/browser/takeover-question-test.mjs`: two runs, 20 checks, passed. Broken by hand (no reload on a jump; the mark ignored): 2 checks failed as they should; restored, product diff empty.
- **Expectations changed**: `tracker-route-test.mjs` (the question's new words; the owner meeting its own session on another device is now told "You are scoring…", accepted beside the named notice).
- **Run**: merged `build/stage-1`; `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, vitest of tracker, core games and `apps/web/src/server` (178 files, 2308 tests) passed; the browser chain in chunks of six, chunks 00 to 10 passed (chunk 09 after the two corrections above). **Not run** (budget): `scoring-plays-test` and `scoring-screen-test`, each a chunk of its own.
- **Distrust**: the browser test moves B's clock, not the server's: "10 minutes" is what B's device reads on its server-clock estimate; the server's real lapse is not exercised. The holder's screen still lags until its next batch answer (T-338 says so). One tap is assumed one event, as T-335 counts.

## Review (independent reviewer, 2026-11-24)

- **High: a play can count twice.** `lost()` takes `madeOn = knownSequence()` (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/tracker-controller.ts:1206`), but the queue's sequence is already advanced by the `session-not-held` answer to the device's own waiting batch (`tracker-queue.ts:491`), and that sequence includes the plays the new holder recorded meanwhile. So when A's queued batch is answered before its renewal (signal back, both race), `notSavedSince` names a sequence after B's plays, the server sees nothing "since", and "Send these plays" adds A's plays on top of B's. If B entered them from the read-out list, they count twice. Shown by a throwaway probe (deleted, not committed): tablet offline with 3 baskets, laptop takes over and scores, tablet's tap is answered before its slowed renewal: send answered `{ ok: true, saved: 4 }`, server 8:2. T-335's "a play never counts twice" is false until fixed. Fix: take the sequence only from answers while holding (or let the server bound `since` by the last sequence it answered to the named session; that also closes the next point).
- **Tests miss it:** `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts:159` and `tests/browser/takeover-question-test.mjs:288` record B's play only after A has learned of the loss. The plan's worst night (B records while A is still offline) is not tested.
- **Medium:** with `notSavedSince` the session check is skipped (`packages/core/src/modules/games/commands/apply-tracker-commands.ts:210-225`); the server trusts the client's sequence, so any account allowed to score that names the current sequence writes plays into a game another device holds, with no takeover and no log entry. Only the honest client stops it.
- **Medium:** under way is `status === 'live'` (`packages/core/src/modules/games/scoring-session.ts:92`). A scorekeeper whose signal went before the first play reached the server is given away after two minutes with no question. T6 §5 says so, but it is the plan's own worst night; asking whenever a lapsed holder exists costs one tap.
- **Medium (outside this step):** `end-tracked-game.ts:63` lets another account end a live game from elsewhere once the lease lapsed, with no question; the silent scorekeeper's plays are then refused.
- **Low:** `game-moved-since.ts:43` matches the plays' own events by command id only, not by account; a batch carrying another person's command ids looks past their events (needs a forged client).
- **Low:** T-338's test (`tracker-controller.ts:1740`) counts taps still in flight in `made`, so a jump is missed until the queue drains (screen lags; the server's count is right). Refused adds are kept as events (record 058) but leave `made` (`:1723`): a needless reload, harmless. By reading, `load()` (`:1315`) neither doubles nor drops a waiting tap; not tested by me.
- **Low:** in `sendNotSaved`, if one batch is taken and the next is unanswered, the retry starts again from the first sequence, so the rest are refused `game-moved` (never twice, but entered again needlessly).
- **Passed review:** `sameAccount` and `context` come from the session (`scorerOf`); a person not allowed to score gets no holder; release on close and mark not started cannot give a game away; the server's lapse is tested with a controlled clock (`open-scoring-session.test.ts:271`). "Enter again" is offered only while holding (S-77), and checked (3 plays) after A takes back. The `tracker-route-test.mjs:675` `.or` is a wait for the page to settle, not a check: acceptable. No waits without a limit in the new browser test.
- **Spec:** T6 §5 and P7 §5.2 match the code (except T-335's claim above). T-335 to T-338 rows have 4 cells, no `|`.
- **Runs:** `takeover-question-test` 20 of 20, `scoring-plays-test` 709, `scoring-screen-test` 1002, all passed.

## Fix round (helper, 2026-11-24)

- **The rule** (T-335 and T6 §5 corrected): the server keeps each session the game was taken from: whose, `heard_seq` (where it last answered it while held: at its start, then every held batch) and `sent_seq` (migration **0027**, numbered 0026 until the closing, `scoring_sessions` gains `heard_seq`, `lost_at`, `sent_seq`; one-per-game is now a unique index `where lost_at is null`). **Lead: the gap check refuses 0027 while 0026 is missing; rename to 0027 and run `npm run db:types` if another lane's 0026 lands first.** Takeover and a lapse given away call `scoringSessions.lose` (row kept), release and mark-not-started still `end`.
- **Where**: `apply-tracker-commands.ts` (the `notSavedSince` branch: `findLost`, same account, then `gameMovedSince` with `heard`/`sent`; every held answer writes `heard`, a taken send writes `sent` and an activity entry `games.apply_tracker_commands` with `change: 'sent-after-takeover'`, the only words the log offers today); `game-moved-since.ts` (since > heard refuses; an event counts only if its account is the sender's and it is one of the batch's ids, an End/reopen, or at or before `sent_seq`). Atomic: the door's `tx.scoringSessions.lockGame(gameId)` (line 186) holds the game to the end of the transaction, and takeovers lock it first too.
- **The device**: `tracker-queue.ts` no longer moves `sequence` on a halted answer and gives subscribers a `HeldAnswer` (`sequence`, `took`); `sendNotSaved` names the same sequence on every batch; T-338 reloads when `answer.sequence - before > answer.took`.
- **Tests, each failed first** (product files swapped back to `bcad8225` and run): `game-moved-since.test.ts` six new (worst night with the waiting batch answered first, forged lower/higher, never held, another account's ids, batches with a lost answer, the log entry): 6 failed. `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts`: the worst night (tablet's renewal slowed until its batch is answered) answered `{ ok: true, saved: 3 }` on the old code; the T-338 first-answer reload and the load with three on their way and one behind them: 2 failed. Session store test now reads holding rows and checks the kept lost row; isolation fixture has a lost session (counts 28 to 29); four new isolation cases, fence check 0 problems.
- **Browser** `takeover-question-test.mjs`: a third run, B records while A is offline; A's send is refused, B's play once, none of A's, "Enter again" ×3. 30 of 30, three times (18 s each).
- **Runs**: `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`; vitest tracker + `apps/web/src/server` + core games (178 files, 2317 tests); `packages/database` isolation (365), schema, transfers, the session/tracker/mark-not-started/role-matrix/end/erase store tests (82 files, 1109). Merged `build/stage-1`: already up to date. **Not run (budget)**: the whole browser chain in chunks.
- **Distrust**: a takeover of a taker forgets nothing now, but a session released (not lost) is not kept, so its plays offer only "Enter again". A refused add is an event the device does not count in `took`: a needless reload. Whether the single named browser run rebuilt the app was not checked by me.

### For the lead

- (i) A scorekeeper whose signal went before the first play reached the server still loses the game after two minutes with no question (`scoring-session.ts:92`, under way is `status === 'live'`).
- (ii) `end-tracked-game.ts:63` ends a live game from elsewhere once the lease lapsed, with no question; its comment calls this deliberate by T-116, I found no decision that weighs it against S-42 (DECISIONS.md not searched, budget).

## Confirming look (2026-11-24)

- **Verdict: sound.** No way found to count a play twice or lose one; every device fault now ends in a refusal and "Enter again", because the server bounds `notSavedSince` by `heard_seq` (`game-moved-since.ts:41`), written in the same transaction under the game's lock (`apply-tracker-commands.ts:187`, `:222`, `:251`, `:267`); takeover, open, renew, release, mark not started and End all lock first.
- **Probed on the real database** (throwaway PGlite test, deleted): held batch then a lost answer (`heard_seq` 2, device knows 1); B records while A is offline: A's send `duplicate` + `game-moved`, a forged later sequence and another scorekeeper both `game-moved`, 3 events. Nothing between: taken once, `sent_seq` 3, a second batch of the list with the same sequence taken, a resend all `duplicate`. Taken twice (A, B, A takes back and scores, B again): the first kept session's plays refused, the second's taken only at its own `heard_seq`.
- **Medium (test gap):** removing the lost session's account check (`apply-tracker-commands.ts:235`) fails no test (452 passed). It is the only thing stopping another scorekeeper who learns a lost session's id from writing plays when nothing was recorded since. Add a test: a second scorekeeper names A's lost session at `heard_seq` with nothing after it.
- **Low:** sessions open when 0027 runs start at `heard_seq` 0, so their first send after a takeover is refused (safe, needless "Enter again"). Kept rows are deleted only when a person is erased (0012 deletes all their sessions); mark not started leaves earlier kept rows, which its own event makes refuse. A refused add, or the duplicates after a lost answer, make T-338 reload needlessly (harmless). A halt only comes from a whole-batch refusal, so a device that still holds is never left on an old sequence.
- **Checked:** `npm run db:types` rewrites nothing; fence check on the 4 new queries, 0 problems; store test 9 passed; migration sound on existing rows (default 0, the partial unique index matches `on conflict ... where lost_at is null`). `since > heard` taken out: 2 tests fail (worst night, forged sequence), restored. `pending-decisions.test.mjs` 11 of 11 (it printed fine). `takeover-question-test` on a fresh build (`BUILD_ID` rewritten during the run): 30 of 30. Still open for the lead: the fix round's (i) and (ii).
